title: Profinite sets as pro-étale $\Spec\Z$-schemes
statement:
Work in the universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal V$ of [def-weil-size-convention], with profinite sets in $\mathcal U$. Let $*_{\mathrm{proét}}$ be the category of profinite sets ([sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]). For a profinite set $S$, let $LC(S,\Z)$ denote the commutative ring of locally constant functions $S\to\Z$, with pointwise operations. Using the spectrum construction [def-weil-affine-spectrum], define
$$u\colon *_{\mathrm{proét}}\longrightarrow(\Spec\Z)_{\mathrm{proét}},\qquad
S\longmapsto\bigl(\Spec LC(S,\Z)\to\Spec\Z\bigr),
$$
where the structure map is induced by the ring homomorphism sending an integer to the corresponding constant function. This takes values in the small pro-étale site of $\Spec\Z$ ([def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]). On morphisms, $u$ sends a continuous map $g\colon S'\to S$ to the morphism $\Spec LC(S',\Z)\to\Spec LC(S,\Z)$ induced by the ring map $LC(S,\Z)\to LC(S',\Z)$, $h\mapsto h\circ g$.

proof.text: Use the universes fixed by [def-weil-size-convention] and the profinite-set source category of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. The functions $S\to\Z$ form a $\mathcal U$-small set. The locally constant functions form a subring: around any point, intersect neighborhoods on which two given functions are constant to see that their sum and product are constant there; negation and the constant functions are locally constant as well. Thus $LC(S,\Z)$ is a concrete commutative ring in $\mathcal U$. Let $c_S:\Z\to LC(S,\Z)$ send $n$ to the constant function with value $n$.

source.place: Construction implicit in the statement; ring of locally constant functions

proof.text: By [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $\Spec LC(S,\Z)$ is a scheme and $\Spec(c_S)$ is its specified morphism to $\Spec\Z$. It is $\mathcal U$-small: prime ideals and the Zariski opens are subsets of power sets of the $\mathcal U$-small ring, and the usual localization rings and sheaf data remain in $\mathcal U$. Apply [lem-sfb-lc-weakly-etale] to this profinite $S$ and exactly this ring of locally constant integer-valued functions. It says that this structure morphism is weakly étale. The object description in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] therefore makes $\Spec(c_S)$ an object of $(\Spec\Z)_{\mathrm{proét}}$.

source.place: First sentence: the weakly étale object condition

proof.text: For a continuous map $g:S'\to S$, define $g^*(h)=h\circ g$. If $h$ is constant on an open neighborhood $V$ of $g(s')$, then $h\circ g$ is constant on the open neighborhood $g^{-1}(V)$ of $s'$. Thus precomposition preserves locally constant functions. The equations $(h+k)\circ g=(h\circ g)+(k\circ g)$, $(hk)\circ g=(h\circ g)(k\circ g)$, and $1\circ g=1$ hold pointwise, so $g^*$ is a unital ring homomorphism. Also $g^*\circ c_S=c_{S'}$.

source.place: Second sentence: precomposition is a well-defined ring map

proof.text: Apply the contravariant functorial spectrum construction of [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and set $u(g)=\Spec(g^*)$. The equality $g^*\circ c_S=c_{S'}$ gives $\Spec(c_S)\circ u(g)=\Spec(c_{S'})$, so this is a morphism over $\Spec\Z$, hence a morphism in the site by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For $g:S'\to S$ and $k:S''\to S'$, the pointwise equations $(\mathrm{id}_S)^*=\mathrm{id}_{LC(S,\Z)}$ and $(g\circ k)^*=k^*\circ g^*$ imply $u(\mathrm{id}_S)=\mathrm{id}_{u(S)}$ and $u(g\circ k)=u(g)\circ u(k)$ by spectrum functoriality. This proves the functor laws, including their direction, for the concrete assignments in the statement.

source.place: Third and fourth sentences: over-base morphisms and functor laws

proof_origin.place: Complete proof paragraph, with the ring-map and functor-law calculations expanded

lean.statement: noncomputable def profiniteToProEt : Profinite.{u} ⥤ specZ.{u}.ProEt where
lean.note: The published pro-etale framework defines exactly this functor. Its object map is ProEt.mk (toSpecZ (profiniteToScheme.obj S)), where profiniteToScheme.obj S is Spec (LocallyConstant S ℤ); its morphism map is induced by LocallyConstant.comapRingHom on precomposition, and comp_toSpecZ proves the morphisms lie over Spec ℤ. The declaration therefore matches the node construction and variance, including the small pro-etale target.
